name: DRAFT (From Exploration to Mastery)
institution: Renmin University of China (Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence) & Baidu Inc.
what_evolved: Context记忆与提示 — evolves the natural-language tool documentation/docstrings (descriptions + parameters) fed to LLMs as context, NOT model weights nor the tool code itself.
skill_as_artifact: Yes — the refined tool documentation is an independent, reusable textual artifact (per-tool JSON: name/description/parameters), portable and shared across different LLMs (cross-model).
skill_encoding: 自然语言 (structured natural-language tool documentation / docstrings; JSON-formatted with description and parameter fields).
skill_granularity: Per-tool usage documentation at the insight/guideline level (clarifies purpose, parameters, response fields, edge cases, and usage examples for a single tool).
how_method: rollout_optimization (non-gradient, text-space iterative rewriting) + reward-based textual feedback: a self-driven trial-and-error loop with three roles — Explorer (generates diverse tool-use trials), Analyzer (LLM-as-judge that performs credit assignment, attributing failures to specific documentation deficiencies and emitting natural-language rather than scalar suggestions), Rewriter (updates the docstring). Includes diversity-promoting exploration (cosine-similarity constraint + self-reflection) and tool-adaptive termination.
learning_signal_source: 成败轨迹 (tool execution outcomes / return results from trials) + 自我反思 (Explorer self-reflection on duplicate queries) + LLM-as-judge (Analyzer critiques documentation vs. execution feedback).
learning_paradigm: offline (documentation library refined before inference); on-policy (backbone refines docs using its own tool-usage feedback).
when_evolve: inter-test-time (offline refinement of the tool-documentation library prior to downstream inference).
trigger: Periodic/iteration-driven (fixed max 5 rounds) combined with convergence-based termination (tool-adaptive stop when consecutive-doc similarity Δ > τ).
library_structure: 扁平 (flat set of per-tool documentation files; one revised doc per tool).
retrieval_method: Direct reuse — refined tool docs are placed verbatim as in-context documentation for the agent at inference (no semantic skill retrieval).
validation: execution-based (real tool/API execution feedback drives each trial) + validation gating (tool-adaptive termination via BLEU + cosine-similarity threshold τ=0.75); downstream eval via Correct Path Rate and Win Rate.
error_correction: self-revision — Rewriter iteratively amends the documentation guided by Analyzer suggestions and execution feedback, with bounded iteration to avoid overfitting.
test_env: tool-call (ToolBench I3-Instruction / RapidAPI, RestBench TMDB & Spotify REST APIs).
backbone_model: GPT-4o (primary DRAFT backbone); also tested Llama-3-70B as backbone; evaluated on GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3-70B.
metrics: success_rate (Correct Path Rate CP%, Win Rate via ChatGPT evaluator), generalization (cross-model transfer of refined docs), cost (token consumption / API cost).
key_results: DRAFT-refined docs preferred by LLMs: RestBench-TMDB 92.5%, RestBench-Spotify 77.5%, ToolBench 87.9%. CP% gains for GPT-4o: TMDB 71→88, Spotify 28.07→70.17, ToolBench 37→51; GPT-4o-mini+DRAFT (CP 47) beats GPT-4o baseline (37) on ToolBench. Robust cross-model generalization (docs refined by one backbone help all models). Ablations confirm both diversity-promoting exploration and tool-adaptive termination contribute; performance peaks then degrades with too many iterations. ICLR 2025 Oral (1.8%).
limitations: scalability (high iterative API cost per tool; expensive for large tool sets), transferability (evaluated only on tool-call benchmarks, no other domains), overfitting risk (performance declines after excessive iterations, mitigated but not eliminated by termination mechanism), backbone-dependence (GPT-4o backbone yields better docs than Llama-3-70B).
